subject: general
question:
In the question four alternatives are given for the underlined word in the sentence. Choose the alternative which best expresses the opposite meaning of the word.

“Well, what if it is? You are not afraid of anything, you know,” returned the boy, looking __wicked__.
solution:
The correct answer is** Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"wicked"** means morally wrong or bad; having or showing a desire to harm others. (दुष्ट)

 
 
• **Example: **The **wicked **witch cast a spell on the entire village.
 
 
 
• **"Righteous" **refers to someone who is morally right or justifiable; virtuous. (धार्मिक)
 
 
• **Example: **He is known for his **righteous** conduct and integrity.
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'wicked'** is **'righteous'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Clean **(स्वच्छ): Free from dirt, marks, or stains.

 
 
• **Example:** She always keeps her house **clean** and tidy.
 
 
 
• **Evil **(बुराई): Profoundly immoral and wicked.
 
 
• **Example: **The** evil** sorcerer plotted against the kingdom.
 
 
 
• **Improper** (अनुचित): Not in accordance with accepted rules or standards.
 
 
• **Example:** His** improper** behavior at the meeting was not appreciated by anyone.
